gold.text: The project manager introduced the agenda and the task of developing an original, trendy, user-friendly remote control through individual work and team meetings.
The participants practiced using the SMARTboard by drawing animals with different colours and line widths and explaining their choices.
The project manager stated a EUR 25 selling price, a EUR 50 million sales aim, and a production allowance of half the selling price.
The team clarified roles: industrial design would address the working design, user interface design the technical functions, and marketing the user requirements.
Participants discussed desirable remote characteristics, including usable button size, a manageable unit and an adequate operating range.
They discussed how requirements research and design responsibilities fit together, and asked whether the remote would control only a television or several devices.
The starting assumption was television and video control, with the possibility of additional features left open.
The meeting ended with individual design/research work and a further functional-design session planned; the project manager also undertook to summarize the discussion in the project folder.
The user interface designer will specify the remote's technical functions.
The marketing expert will research user requirements, using the internet and potentially direct user enquiries.
The industrial designer will develop the working design and bring ideas for discussion at the next meeting.
The project manager expected the team to receive further information by email.
Use EUR 25 as the product selling-price target.
The project manager stated an aim to sell EUR 50 million worth of product.
Allow production costs of half the EUR 25 selling price, i.e. EUR 12.50 per remote.
Use television and video control as a provisional starting scope while reserving the possibility of additional features.
The project manager will summarize the discussion and place it in the project folder.
